1.o: In this chapter we have, I. The introduction to the whole epistle, which is much the same as in others, ver. 1, 2. II. The apostle's thanksgivings and praises to God for his inestimable blessings bestowed on the believing Ephesians, ver. 3-14. III. His earnest prayers to God in their behalf, ver. 15-23.
1.i: Ephesians 1 to 3 hold the doctrine of the letter: chosen by grace, saved by grace, and joined together as one family.
1.p: Father, thank You that we are saved by grace. Build us together into a home where You live. Amen.
1.l: Do one good thing today that you did not have to do, and remember that you were made for it.
q: Ephesus's temple was the pride of the world. What do you point to with pride that Christ is building better?

2.o: This chapter contains an account, I. Of the miserable condition of these Ephesians by nature (ver. 1-3) and again, ver. 11, 12. II. Of the glorious change that was wrought in them by converting grace (ver. 4-10) and again, ver. 13. III. Of the great and mighty privileges that both converted Jews and Gentiles receive from Christ, ver. 14-22.
2.i: Ephesians 1 to 3 hold the doctrine of the letter: chosen by grace, saved by grace, and joined together as one family.
2.p: Father, thank You that we are saved by grace. Build us together into a home where You live. Amen.
2.l: Do one good thing today that you did not have to do, and remember that you were made for it.
q: Ephesus's temple was the pride of the world. What do you point to with pride that Christ is building better?

3.o: This chapter consists of two parts. I. Of the account which Paul gives the Ephesians concerning himself, as he was appointed by God to be the apostle of the Gentiles, ver. 1-13. II. Of his devout and affectionate prayer to God for the Ephesians, ver. 14-21.
3.i: Ephesians 1 to 3 hold the doctrine of the letter: chosen by grace, saved by grace, and joined together as one family.
3.p: Father, thank You that we are saved by grace. Build us together into a home where You live. Amen.
3.l: Do one good thing today that you did not have to do, and remember that you were made for it.
q: Ephesus's temple was the pride of the world. What do you point to with pride that Christ is building better?

4.o: We have gone through the former part of this epistle, which consists of several important doctrinal truths, contained in the three preceding chapters. We enter now on the latter part of it, in which we have the most weighty and serious exhortations that can be given.
4.i: Ephesians 4 and 5 turn from belief to behaviour: one body, a new self, and a walk in love.
4.p: Lord, make us one body. Teach us to speak the truth in love and to put on the new self each morning. Amen.
4.l: If you are upset with someone, make it right before the sun goes down today.
q: 'Evangelist' names a work and not a rank. What work is yours to do whether or not anyone gives you the title?

5.o: We had several important exhortations in the close of the foregoing chapter, and they are continued in this: particularly, I. We have here an exhortation to mutual love and charity, ver. 1, 2. II. Against all manner of uncleanness, with proper arguments and remedies proposed against such sins: and some further cautions are added, and other duties recommended, ver. 3-20. III. The apostle directs to the conscientious discharge of relative duties, from ver.
5.i: Ephesians 4 and 5 turn from belief to behaviour: one body, a new self, and a walk in love.
5.p: Lord, make us one body. Teach us to speak the truth in love and to put on the new self each morning. Amen.
5.l: If you are upset with someone, make it right before the sun goes down today.
q: 'Evangelist' names a work and not a rank. What work is yours to do whether or not anyone gives you the title?

6.o: In this chapter, I. The apostle proceeds in the exhortation to relative duties which he began in the former, particularly he insists on the duties of children and parents, and of servants and masters, ver. 1-9. II. He exhorts and directs Christians how to behave themselves in the spiritual warfare with the enemies of their souls; and to the exercise of several Christian graces, which he proposes to them as so many pieces of spiritual armour, to preserve and defend them in the conflict, ver. 10-18. III.
6.i: Ephesians 6 ends the letter with a picture every reader could see: the soldier fully dressed, ready to stand.
6.p: Lord, clothe us with Your armor: truth, peace, faith and Your word. Help us to stand and to pray. Amen.
6.l: Pick one piece of the armor, such as truth or peace, and try to wear it all day.
q: Paul says to stand, not to charge. When is standing the hardest part?
